title: Galaxies and the Milky Way
examples: What is the difference between a spiral and an elliptical galaxy?
How big is our galaxy, the Milky Way?
Are all galaxies shaped like spirals?

explain.say: Today we will learn about different kinds of galaxies.
Some galaxies have arms that spin out from a center.
These galaxies look like big, smooth, football shapes.
Some galaxies do not fit into a clear pattern or shape.
Our galaxy, the Milky Way, is a spiral galaxy.
In our galaxy, most stars are located within the disk.

draw.text: Milky Way: Stars in the disk

faq.q: What is the Milky Way galaxy?
faq.a: The Milky Way is the galaxy that contains our solar system. It is classified as a spiral galaxy.
asks: Which galaxy do we live in?
What type of galaxy is our home?

faq.a: No, galaxies can take many different shapes. They can also be elliptical or irregular.
asks: What other shapes do galaxies have?

faq.q: What is the difference between spiral and elliptical?
faq.a: Spiral galaxies have distinct arms rotating around a center. Elliptical galaxies are smoother and more like a football.
asks: Spiral vs elliptical, what's the key difference?

faq.q: Where is the Sun located in the Milky Way?
faq.a: Our Sun is located within the disk of the Milky Way galaxy. It is not at the very center.
asks: Is the Sun at the center of the galaxy?
What part of the Milky Way is the Sun in?

faq.q: What does 'irregular' mean for a galaxy?
faq.a: An irregular galaxy does not have a clear, recognizable shape. It often results from gravitational interactions.
asks: What is a galaxy without a shape?
Why are some galaxies messy looking?

facts: Spiral galaxies are characterized by distinct arms rotating around a central bulge.
Elliptical galaxies are generally smooth and range in size from small to very large.
The Milky Way galaxy is believed to be a barred spiral galaxy.
Irregular galaxies do not fit neatly into the spiral or elliptical classifications.

quiz.say: A galaxy with arms spinning around a center is most likely:
quiz.why: Spiral galaxies are defined by their visible, rotating arms.

wrong.0: Irregular galaxies do not follow any predictable shape.
wrong.1: Disk describes a location, not the overall galaxy shape.
wrong.3: Elliptical galaxies are smooth and lack defined arms.

quiz.say: If a galaxy is smooth and round, it is probably a:
quiz.why: Elliptical galaxies are known for their smooth, egg-like appearance.

wrong.1: Spiral galaxies show clear, rotating structures.
wrong.2: Irregular galaxies are defined by having no set shape.
wrong.3: Milky Way is a specific name, not a general shape type.

quiz.say: Our galaxy, the Milky Way, is an example of which type?
quiz.why: The Milky Way is observed to have the characteristic spiral structure.

wrong.0: The Milky Way has a very clear, organized pattern.
wrong.1: The Milky Way fits the definition of a spiral galaxy.
wrong.3: This shape is too smooth for the Milky Way's structure.
